summary: Steel fire tower about 1.25 miles north of Dagsboro, Sussex County, Delaware, built in 1931 and removed between 2002 and 2006.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with a 7-foot square cabin, upper half glass-enclosed
facts.status_note: Removed between 2002 and 2006; no source describes what remains on the site
facts.agency: State Forestry Commission (per the state forester's annual reports)

events.note: Built in 1931 per the FFLA page; the state forester's report dates the erection of the towers from July 29 to October 15, 1931
Wind erosion of the sandy soil around the piers; fenced and planted with pine seedlings in 1932 and 1933, loam fill in 1934
Original window sash replaced with new cypress sash
Extensive repairs to steps and landings
Removed between 2002 and 2006; the year shown is the start of that range. Turned over to the State Police for communications purposes before removal
Added to the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 11, 2008

corrections.why: The 1931 state forester report gives 100 feet from ground to cabin floor (110 feet overall) for these steel towers. 10.7 m is about 35 feet, the site elevation the same report gives. Needs a human check.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: DE 1 appears in two registers: Dagsboro is FFLOS US 70, DE 1, while the NHLR's DE 1 entry is listed for Smyrna (US 52, DE 1). The shared label does not change Dagsboro's own number.

notes_for_editor: The record height_m of 10.7 m (about 35 ft) looks like the 35-foot site elevation in the 1931 report. The proposed 30.5 m (100 ft to the cabin floor) is in corrections for human review; the report describes the towers as a group, and the Dagsboro passage sits within it. Elevation differs: FFLOS gives 26 ft (8 m, matching record 7.9 m); the 1931 report gives a 35-foot elevation. Coordinates: FFLOS N 38.558830, W 75.250330 vs record and firelookout.org 38.56472, -75.25056, about 650 m apart; record kept, not corrected. The 1931 build date comes from the FFA page; the report gives erection dates for the group. No source describes the site today, so access is omitted. Staffing is limited to the open-season sentence. A January 2002 photo by Gary Weber is captioned on the FFA Dagsboro page; it was not downloaded and no license was checked, so none is added. A DNREC PDF about a former Dagsboro substation on Kollock Street came up in search; it is a different site and was not used.
